newsitem.title: ITALY: Judge rejects bid to free Italy rail chief.
newsitem.headline: Judge rejects bid to free Italy rail chief.

text.p: A judge ruled on Monday that the chief of Italy's state railway, implicated in a growing corruption probe, must remain in jail while the case continues.

The preliminary investigating judge in this northwestern port town rejected a request by defence lawyers to free Ferrovie dello Stato (FS) managing director Lorenzo Necci, held under pre-trial detention since September 15.

Necci, a respected public administrator, was the first person to be arrested in the probe, which the media have named "Tangentopoli (Bribesville) 2" after a corruption scandal which broke in 1992 and toppled Italy's old political guard.
Since Necci's arrest, the probe has mushroomed to include judges, businessmen and lawyers as magistrates look into allegations of trial-fixing and bribes for state contracts.
Newspapers on Sunday published transcripts of wiretaps which investigators believe point to illegal arms trafficking to a number of countries including Iraq and Bosnia.
President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro, in a speech on Sunday night in the northern city of Turin, acknowledged that "a serious wound had been re-opened in our country" by the new probe.
But he said the magistrates should continue their work, saying: "A scalpel was needed to save the healthy part" of Italy.
Defence lawyers said the judge did not immediately publish his reasons for rejecting the bid for Necci's release.
